headlines: Four mountain bongos from a Czech zoo have touched Kenyan soil, joining efforts to restore a species down to fewer than fifty individuals in the wild.
Conservators in southern Iraq are hand-making mud bricks to restore the 4,000-year-old Ziggurat of Ur, matching the original clay chemistry one brick at a time.
An oral antiviral taken within three days of household exposure cuts the risk of developing COVID-19 by two-thirds, a Phase 3 trial found.
New HIV infections have fallen 40 percent worldwide since 2010, with the African region recording a 70 percent drop in AIDS-related deaths since the 2005 peak.
A 3.5 mm wasp that spent 40 years unsorted in a museum drawer turned out to be an entirely new genus — named after David Attenborough on his 100th birthday.
A retired gym teacher in Moncton has spent 14 years collecting and repairing donated bicycles so no child who cannot afford one goes without.
Hundreds of wild asses are grazing in eastern Mongolia again after a sixty-five-year absence.
Five hundred freshwater turtles are swimming again after an Australian community raised A$100,000 to keep their lake alive.
Tunisia has eliminated trachoma, ending a disease that once blinded at least half its population.
Hard-ground barasingha are thriving in two new reserves, ending a century of existing in only one place.
Hanoi has taken the fences down from its public parks and given them back to the street.
Engineered algae can pull nine-tenths of microplastics out of water in under an hour.
Scotland's first community-won marine reserve now holds twice as many species as the unprotected sea beside it.
A targeted drug roughly doubles survival time for the most common form of pancreatic cancer.
Wellingtonians finished returning 250 kiwi to hills where none had called at night for a century.
Larvae of a butterfly absent from Britain for a century are feeding well on Sussex hawthorn.
A Polish streamer ran nine days and raised $76 million — more than triple the world record.
Ghana has protected its first marine reserve — 703 square kilometres of West African coastline.
sources: University of Exeter / Convex Seascape Survey

headlines: Nine hundred observers in Indonesian Borneo now earn money photographing wildlife, and informal hunting bans are forming.
An 800-year-old sequence of eight movements lowers blood pressure as well as a first-line drug.
A stainless steel built for seawater could cut the main material cost of green hydrogen forty times.
